terms.comment: “The clear-sounding pipe”, from the classical clārisonus (Catull. 64.320); “play the clarinet” is tībiā clārisonā canere. Traupman marks the i long; Lewis & Short has it short.
The modern name in Latin form. Morgan–Owens marks only the long e; Andresian also marks the i long (clārīnēta), which nothing else supports.
“The single-reed pipe”, beside Morgan–Owens’s tībia bicalama for the oboe; ūnicalamus is Pliny’s word for a single-stemmed plant.

clarisona.html: Lewis & Short clārĭsŏnus; the compound vowel is the short connecting -i- of clāri-sonus, as in horri-sonus, alti-sonus.
